cards.text: This song comes from Asaph, the Levite David made chief of the worship music (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He opens with a prayer to God, with no warm-up and no small talk. He goes STRAIGHT to it, friend.

cards.question: Asaph opens by asking God the same thing three different ways. What is he asking God not to be?

cards.text: Then Asaph points God to what's going on: "See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads." That's not a quiet prayer, friend, that's me yelling across the bakery when I see smoke pouring out of an oven.

cards.question: These raging enemies scheme with cunning. Asaph says they're plotting against God's ___.
The enemies have a plan, and Asaph quotes it. What do they say they want to do to Israel?

cards.text: "Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more." Friend, I spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody was working THAT hard at it.

cards.question: Asaph says the nations plotting against Israel can't agree on a plan.
These nations plot together with one mind and form an alliance. Who does Asaph say the alliance is against?

cards.text: Then Asaph names ten who are in on it, from Edom, Moab and Ammon to Philistia and Tyre, all the way to Assyria, lending strength to the sons of Lot. That's not an alliance, friend, that's a GROUP CHAT with only one topic.

Asaph's got a whole crowd lined up against God's people, so he pulls out the receipts, OLD ones: Midian, and Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon. Back in Israel's past, Midian's army fled before Gideon's three hundred (Judges 7:19-22), and the LORD routed Sisera, commander of King Jabin's army (Judges 4:2, 15).

cards.question: Asaph brings up Midian, Sisera and Jabin. What is he asking God to do to today's enemies?

answers.text: Defeat them like He defeated those enemies
Send them back to their own lands

cards.text: Asaph does NOT soften it, friend: they perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground. Then he asks God to make today's nobles and princes like four leaders of Midian: Oreb and Zeeb (Judges 7:25), Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:5).

cards.question: Right after those names, Asaph quotes some people who wanted to possess something for themselves. What was it?

cards.text: Then Asaph trades the history lesson for pictures: "Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind."

cards.question: Tumbleweed and chaff before the wind. Asaph is asking God to make the enemies easy to ___ away.

cards.text: Like crumbs on my counter when I blow on them, FWOOSH, gone. Then the next picture: fire eating up a forest, and a flame setting the mountains ablaze.

cards.question: After the fire picture, Asaph asks God to chase the enemies down with a flood.

cards.text: No flood. Just like fire sweeping the mountains, Asaph says, "so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm."
Then the prayer takes a turn I did NOT see coming. Asaph asks God to cover their faces with shame, and he says what it's for.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to cover the enemies' faces with shame. Why?

answers.text: So they may seek the LORD's name
So Israel can laugh at them

cards.question: After praying that the enemies seek the LORD's name, Asaph stops asking for them to be ashamed.

cards.text: Next line: "May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace." Asaph is not done, friend, he is NOT done, and his very last line is about what he wants them to know.

cards.question: Asaph ends his prayer with what he wants the enemies to know. What is it?

answers.text: That the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth
That Israel will rule over every nation on earth
That Asaph's prayers are always heard in heaven
